title: Service Forensics Playbook — Causation Reconstruction & Traffic Replay
author: Evelyn Chen
content:
Summary:

This playbook defines a repeatable, low-friction process for collecting, preserving, and replaying production traffic and service state to reconstruct root cause for service incidents. It focuses on: collecting high-fidelity evidence, persisting model-serving and cache state, performing deterministic replays in a sandbox, and tying findings back to SLOs and capacity signals.

Scope:
- Services: inference runtime, request-router, kv-cache-layer, autoscaler, routing-proxy.
- Activities covered: pre-incident instrumentation, live evidence collection, post-incident replay & causation analysis, evidence packaging and retention.
- Not covered: legal subpoena handling (see security-and-compliance).

Definitions:
- Incident ID: unique id = YYYYMMDD-service-short-#### (e.g., 20260305-runtime-0042).
- Replay sandbox: isolated environment with identical service binaries/config but mocked downstreams.
- Deterministic replay: replay where inputs, random seeds, and cache populations are controlled to reproduce behavior within expected statistical variance.

Pre-incident instrumentation checklist (owner: observability):
- Trace sampling: ensure 100% header capture for emergency traces (header-only trace tags) and 10% detailed traces by default.
- Short-lived request snapshots: sample 1:100 requests + capture full request/response bodies for sampled ids; rotate sensitive fields via PII scrubbing.
- KV cache checkpointing: configure periodic checkpoints of prefix/KV caches to S3 using rwd-kv-dump (every 10 minutes for high-throughput services).
- Model state snapshots: for models with ephemeral weights/embeddings, enable model-metadata export on crash (model name, version, quantization profile).
- Metrics: export p50/p95/p99 latencies, error counts, 5m QPS, CPU/GPU util, retry counts at 1s granularity to Prometheus/long-term store.
- Canary toggles: keep canary traffic routing flags in feature-flag service and snapshot states.

During incident: immediate evidence collection (ordered checklist for oncall):
1) Assign Incident ID and create incident folder: s3://redwood-incident-evidence/<incident-id>/ (owner: oncall).
2) Freeze ephemeral retention policies for the incident (observability) to prevent automatic log deletion.
3) Capture timeline (first 30 minutes): collect system clock-synced timeline entries from:
   - Tracing: all traces flowed through /traces/collect?incident=<id> (use 100% header capture).
   - Logs: journalctl/k8s logs for affected pods (±30 minutes).
   - Metrics snapshot: Prometheus 5m and 1m series export around incident start.
4) Preserve KV and prefix cache: run rwd-kv-dump --namespace <service> --since <incident-start-30m> --out s3://.../kv-dumps/<pod>-<ts>.tar.gz.
5) Export model-serving runtime state: rwd-runtime-dump --pod <pod> --out s3://.../model-dumps/<pod>-<ts>.json (includes model_version, quant_profile, active_kv_ms).
6) Network captures: capture tcpdump for a 10 minute window for affected nodes: tcpdump -w /tmp/incident-<id>-<node>.pcap and upload to S3.
7) Snapshot routing and config: dump the routing table and autoscaler decisions: rwd-routerctl snapshot > /tmp/router-snapshot.json.

Evidence packaging guidance:
- Maintain a manifest file at s3://redwood-incident-evidence/<incident-id>/MANIFEST.json listing file paths, checksums (sha256), collection time (ISO 8601), and owner.
- Tag all artifacts with incident-id, service, pod id, and relative timestamp.

Data retention and storage requirements (table):
| Artifact | Storage location | Minimum retention | Owner | Format |
|---------|------------------|-------------------|-------|--------|
| Traces (full) | S3 /traces/<incident-id>/ | 90 days | observability | jaeger/zipkin JSON |
| Logs (raw) | S3 /logs/<incident-id>/ | 180 days | observability | line-delimited JSON |
| KV dumps | S3 /kv-dumps/<incident-id>/ | 365 days | platform | tar.gz (rwd-kv-dump) |
| Model runtime dumps | S3 /model-dumps/<incident-id>/ | 365 days | runtime | JSON |
| PCAPs | S3 /pcap/<incident-id>/ | 90 days | platform | pcap |
| Replay inputs | S3 /replay-inputs/<incident-id>/ | 365 days | oncall | ndjson |

Reconstruction & replay procedure (owner: platform + runtime):
1) Prepare replay sandbox:
   - Provision a dedicated replay namespace with the same binaries (git tag) and identical config (feature flags, quantization profile).
   - Mock downstream services and external dependencies to avoid side effects (use rwd-mock-proxy).
2) Restore KV state: load the KV dump: rwd-kv-load --namespace <service> --file s3://.../kv-dumps/<file>.tar.gz --force-populate.
3) Seed model runtime: restore model metadata and active state using rwd-runtime-restore --file s3://.../model-dumps/<file>.json.
4) Run deterministic replay engine: rwd-replay --inputs s3://.../replay-inputs/<incident-id>/ --retries 0 --preserve-headers --seed <incident-seed> --concurrency <x> --out s3://.../replay-results/<incident-id>/.
   Example: rwd-replay --inputs s3://redwood-incident-evidence/20260305-runtime-0042/replay-inputs.ndjson --seed 20260305-0042 --concurrency 8
5) Acceptance criteria for a successful replay run (must be met before concluding causation):
   - Latency distribution replication: p50/p95/p99 delta <= 10% against production window baseline.
   - Error signature match: same error types and stack traces in >= 80% of failing traces.
   - Resource signal parity: GPU utilization and memory pressure within ±15% of production incident window.
   - Determinism signal: re-run of the same input batch yields same outputs (byte-for-byte or within tolerated stochastic variance for model outputs).
6) If criteria not met, iterate: adjust seed, increase cache population window, or broaden input sampling. Document each iteration in MANIFEST.

Common replay troubleshooting scenarios and mitigations:
- Divergent outputs due to stochastic model behavior: fix by setting deterministic RNG seeds (rwd-replay --force-seed) and using the same quantization profile.
- Missing cache-population: replay warmup traffic at low QPS for 10–30 minutes to build prefix/KV state before main replay.
- Side-effectful downstreams: if a dependency cannot be mocked, use recorded responses (rwd-mock-proxy --replay-responses s3://...).

Prometheus/observability quick hits (examples):
- Query for dramatic error budget burn: increase in error_rate over baseline:
  - promQL: sum(increase(runtime_request_errors_total{service="runtime"}[1h])) / sum(increase(runtime_requests_total{service="runtime"}[1h]))
- P99 latency spike across pods:
  - promQL: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(runtime_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, pod))
- Identify pods with highest 5m retry counts:
  - promQL: topk(5, sum(rate(runtime_retries_total[5m])) by (pod))

Roles & responsibilities (quick reference):
- Oncall (first 60 min): assign ID, gather initial evidence, run initial rwd-kv-dump and rwd-runtime-dump, set retention freeze.
- Observability team: provide trace & metrics exports, unlock archives, and assist with promQL extraction.
- Platform team: provision replay sandbox, restore KV and model state, run rwd-replay.
- Runtime team: interpret logs/model traces, analyze stack traces, and validate acceptance criteria.
- Post-incident lead: own RCA writeup, issue remediation tasks, and track SLO/error-budget impacts.

SLO & error budget tie-ins (operational thresholds):
- Example SLOs to monitor during analysis:
  - request success: 99.95% rolling-30d (target); alert if 30d rolling < 99.8% (severity-2).
  - p99 latency: < 250 ms for interactive endpoints; alert if p99 > 350 ms for 10m.
- Error budget policies during replay: do not use production capacity for large-scale replays if 30-day error budget < 20% remaining. Use replay sandbox and throttled inputs.

Evidence closure and retro requirements:
1) Package MANIFEST and a short "replay summary" that includes the replay seed(s), number of inputs, acceptance metrics and diff artifacts.
2) Upload artifacts to incident folder and add links to the incident ticket.
3) Postmortem: include a section "Replay findings" with deterministic evidence and recommended remediation steps.

Tooling & example commands (reference):
- rwd-kv-dump --namespace runtime --since "2026-03-05T12:34:00Z" --out s3://redwood-incident-evidence/20260305-runtime-0042/kv-dumps/pod-7.tar.gz
- rwd-runtime-dump --pod runtime-7 --out s3://redwood-incident-evidence/20260305-runtime-0042/model-dumps/runtime-7.json
- rwd-kv-load --namespace runtime --file s3://.../pod-7.tar.gz --confirm
- rwd-replay --inputs s3://.../replay-inputs.ndjson --seed 20260305-0042 --concurrency 8 --preserve-headers
- promtool query examples included above.

Acceptance & sign-off (incident lead):
- Evidence completeness verified: MANIFEST has all items + checksums.
- Replay acceptance criteria met OR explicit note about why deterministic replay could not be performed.
- Postmortem includes a prioritized remediation plan with owners and ETA.

References:
- Observability runbook: /confluence/eng-sre/operational-tooling/sre-rotation-automation-and-capacity-signal-playbook-2026
- Capacity playbook: /confluence/eng-sre/capacity-planning/service-capacity-governance-and-error-budget-handbook-2025

Attachments and templates:
- Incident MANIFEST template (JSON) and replay summary template are stored at s3://redwood-doc-templates/forensics-templates/.

Notes & best practices:
- Keep replays out of production; always use sandboxed infrastructure unless a surgical, small-scope verification is necessary and approved by SRE lead.
- Scrub PII at collection time using approved scrubbing rules.
- When in doubt, collect more artifacts: storage is cheaper than lost evidence.
